label: digit 1 input during the original phase
explanation: Token feature: fires whenever the input is the digit 1 while the original sequence is being read (t < L), at any position and any L. It essentially never fires on 1 when it comes back as input in the copy phase (20 activations in the dev split), and never fires on other tokens or at the delimiter. Magnitude is highest for a 1 at the first step (about 1.0 of max) and gets weaker for 1s later in the sequence. A repeated 1 (one already seen earlier) fires much more weakly, about 0.1 to 0.6 of max.

issues: Minor magnitude imprecision: the explanation says a repeated 1 fires at about 0.1 to 0.6 of max, but dev examples show repeats at 0.73 ('1 n t a [1:0.73]'), 0.81 ('1 s w [1:0.81] z') and 0.75 ('1 3 3 [1:0.75]'). So repeats range up to about 0.8, especially when the earlier 1 is close or the repeat comes early. The overall pattern (repeats are weaker, magnitude falls with position) holds: first 1s go from 1.00 at t=0 to about 0.4-0.6 at t=5-7, and in_first=0 holds only 6.9% of activation mass.

Test split: P=0.99967, R=0.99968, F1=0.99968, mass recall 0.999996. All 34 test misses are copy-phase 1s with activation 0.00-0.03 (0% of mass), right after a sequence that starts with 1. All 36 test false positives are a 1 at the last original step t=8 (L=9). These are tiny, low-mass edge cases, not a systematic class worth adding to the predicate.
Factual claims checked against the dev profile: 0 activations at the delimiter; 20 in the copy phase (recall_idx=1 only); 0 on any token other than 1; firing rate is flat across L and orig_idx.
